decision-tree.root-question: How many functions does the proposed starter suite contain, and does it cover all five categories (performance, deployability, dependency structure, complexity, contract)?

branch.conclusion: Cut or extend to 5 to 8 functions with at least one per category before wiring anything into CI.
Add a p95 latency function on one critical endpoint under a fixed load profile, on a dedicated runner, scheduled post-merge.
Add a pipeline-duration or merge-to-production lead-time function computed from CI timestamps by a committed script.
Add a structural function with ArchUnit, NetArchTest, dependency-cruiser or import-linter enforcing the written dependency graph.
Add a per-function cyclomatic complexity check with a committed baseline of current violators.
Add Pact verification or a breaking-change schema diff against the last released API definition.

branch.question: Are all functions in informational or ratchet mode with a recorded baseline, a named owner each, and the four weekly reviews scheduled?

branch.conclusion: Demote to informational or ratchet; promote to blocking only after five green runs on main and the first weekly review.
Assign one owner per function and put the four weekly reviews on the calendar before launch.
The bootstrap is done; further changes belong to the ongoing suite review, not to this methodology.

example.p: Six functions proposed: ArchUnit layers, radon complexity, k6 p95, pipeline duration, Pact verification, dependency CVE scan. All categories covered, but every job is blocking with no baseline. shape == 'complete', rollout == 'blocking_uncalibrated' → conclusion r-ffsb-ratchet-first-then-block.
